key_insight: Adding clouds and fast phase changes to rotating stratified flow reduces but does not eliminate inverse energy transfer, while generating large-scale coherent moist PV structures tied to cloud boundaries.
engineering_relevance: The results matter for geophysical and climate simulations because moisture and phase transitions can alter upscale energy transfer, coherence, and large-scale circulation even when rotation and stratification are strong.
method: Numerical simulations of a Boussinesq rotating-stratified model with water vapor and liquid water.
Random forcing with asymptotically fast cloud microphysics to study inverse transfer.
Comparison of dry versus moist cases using Rossby number and separate Froude numbers for unsaturated and saturated regions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed energy transfer rates and statistical relationships between cloud-phase boundaries, updrafts/downdrafts, and moist potential vorticity in flow regions dominated by moist PV vortices.
watch_item: The model is idealized and relies on asymptotically fast microphysics, so direct quantitative transfer to real clouds may depend on unresolved microphysical and multiscale effects.
paper_title: Inverse Transfer and Coherence in Rotating Stratified Flow with Clouds and Phase Transitions
